angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 591,345 km at 82.52 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.1190 +/- 0.0117 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 82.52 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.85 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Murgas et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-283 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.201M/abstract): 591,345 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.8 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Murgas et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-283 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.201M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5213 +/- 70 K from Murgas et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-283 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.201M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Murgas et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-283 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...703A.201M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-283.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.482, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
